title: X Feed Digest

summary.html: Model quality was not the main story — deployment economics were: DeepSeek's discounting, GPT-5.5's effective coding cost, and Codex quota complaints kept turning model choice into a budgeting decision.

summary: Agent infrastructure kept moving downstack: Google launched a managed enterprise agent platform, Cua shipped background macOS control, and acpx continued tightening the control plane around coding-agent sessions.

The most useful workflow ideas were practical rather than flashy: separate human-to-human from AI-to-AI communication, treat queue triage as the first believable always-on agent job, and design internal tools that computer-use agents can actually navigate.
Research chatter also pushed against brute-force scaling as the only path forward, with MIT's recursive long-context approach drawing attention as an alternative to endlessly larger context windows.

items.title: @berryxia: MIT's RLM Attacks Context Rot
items.body: A thread on MIT CSAIL's Recursive Language Models argued that long-context work may be better handled by external state, selective retrieval, and recursive sub-agents than by endlessly expanding native windows. If the implementation holds up, it's a real challenge to the idea that bigger context windows are the only path to stronger long-horizon agents.

items.title: @googlecloud: Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform
items.body: Google launched Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform as a managed layer to build, govern, optimize, and scale agents inside enterprise workflows. The bigger signal is that agent orchestration and governance are becoming a first-class platform category, not just a feature bolted onto models.

items.title: @0xLogicrw: Background Mac Control For Agents
items.body: Cua's new macOS-native driver lets agents click, type, inspect UI, and capture context in the background without stealing focus or moving the user's cursor. That's meaningful infrastructure for desktop agents because it makes computer use less of a demo and more compatible with normal daily work.

items.title: @steipete: acpx 0.6.0 Tightens Agent Control
items.body: acpx 0.6.0 shipped better session pruning, queue hardening, persistent-session fixes, and improved controls for running Codex and Claude through agents. For anyone turning coding agents into real tooling, this kind of orchestration plumbing matters more than another benchmark screenshot.

items.title: @fkysly: Codex Can Import Claude Code Setup
items.body: Starting a project in Codex now offers a one-click migration path for Claude Code settings, skills, and Claude.md content into Agents.md. That meaningfully lowers switching friction for teams that want to test GPT-5.5 and Codex without rebuilding their whole environment from scratch.

items.title: @xiaohu: DeepSeek V4 Slashes Output Pricing
items.body: A temporary DeepSeek V4 promotion cut output pricing by roughly 75% to about RMB 6 per million tokens, underscoring how quickly open-model competition is turning into a pricing war. If you're routing workloads across models, this is the kind of change that can justify revisiting defaults immediately.

items.title: @xiongchun007: GPT-5.5's Real Coding Cost Looks Higher
items.body: One useful pricing read argued that GPT-5.5's headline API rate understates what coding-agent usage can feel like once hidden reasoning and worst-case paths are included. The practical takeaway is to budget around effective cost, not just the clean price card.

items.title: @Sauers_: Codex Can Burn Through Weekly Quota Fast
items.body: A heavy user said Codex consumed an entire ChatGPT Pro weekly allowance in one day and still ran into shorter-term rate limits and errors. Even when model quality is strong, quota ceilings are becoming part of the real economics of agent-heavy workflows.

items.title: @FranWalsh73: Gifted Stock vs Inheritance Tax Gap
items.body: The post resurfaced a classic estate-planning lesson: gifting appreciated stock during life can create a large capital-gains bill, while passing the same asset through inheritance may receive a step-up in basis. It's a useful reminder that tax treatment can matter more than the size of the gift itself.

items.title: @jiayq: Keep Human Thinking Separate From AI Output
items.body: A clean collaboration rule: don't forward AI-written prose as if it were your own thinking — send the prompt or your raw reasoning instead, and keep human-to-human versus AI-to-AI channels distinct. That's one of the sharper norms in the batch for keeping team communication useful.

items.title: @Voxyz_ai: 50-Agent Triage Is A Reusable Pattern
items.body: The '50 agents cleaning 4,000 stale issues' story was framed less as a flex and more as a queue-triage pattern for resumes, support, sales leads, inboxes, and moderation. The important insight is that always-on agents look most believable when they are screening queues, not pretending to be autonomous geniuses.

items.title: @tualatrix: Build Internal Tools For Computer Use
items.body: After watching Codex's computer-use agent struggle with a private admin tool, the author concluded the bigger problem was the UI rather than the model. It's a sharp reminder that agents expose interfaces that only make sense to their creators, which is now a real product-design concern.

items.title: @bearliu: Stop Using Humans As Glue
items.body: Reflecting on Notion CEO Ivan Zhao's recent essay, this post argued that the biggest productivity gain comes when teams stop using humans as glue between systems and redesign workflows around agents. The useful lesson is less 'use more AI' and more 'change the operating model AI is sitting inside.'
